docs.text:

Essentials →

  • highest mobility
  • high CD gem investment
  • stimulant recommended

📚 Additional Resources

Shared by both playstyles: bonus skill codes, calculators and useful links.

Calculators Useful Links

Reading the names

333, 313, 111, 222 are shorthand for each build's Ark Grid Core assignment.

Trixion DPS is the build's measured DPS multiplier against a dummy target.

About

This site adapts KR Deathblade research for NA.

You can fork the repo to build a guide for this or another class.

docs.title: 111 (Head Hunt) 🔪
docs.text:
Best For: Players who want maximum skill expression and speed.

Tradeoff: Unforgiving rotation with very little room for error.

  • This is the final form of the old-school Remaining Energy gameplay.
  • Head Hunt is used in the rotation, so it may not be available for counter.
  • Lower orb generation and fewer recovery options than Fatal Wave builds.

docs.title: Skill Setup

TipRunes
  • Use Purify on Head Hunt if absolutely necessary.
NoteOptions & Tripods
  • You can use Swift Fingers tripod on Blitz Rush for increased DPS and QoL.
    • It's a DPC loss unless you can make use of the increased CPM/comfort.
    • It's not compatible with very low Specialization or a +CD% bracelet line.

    • Set Void Strike to Lv 13 and Blitz Rush to Lv 12 if you decide to use this tripod.

docs.title: Rotation
docs.text:
Use an opener (optional), then alternate between Cycle 1 and Cycle 2 as needed for the rest of the encounter.

The opener stacks Adrenaline and applies synergies efficiently. If it feels overwhelming, just apply synergy and Surge.

Opener from 3 orbs (Stimulant)

  1. If available, Blade Assault is interchangeable with Cycle 2.
  2. It's efficient to use Atropine after Deathly Slash, with Blade Assault available.

Alternating cycles

1Void Strike + Deathly Slash Cycle 2Soul Absorber + Blitz Rush Cycle
  1. Aim to fit up to Cycle 2's Twin Shadows under Cycle 1's Maelstrom to reach 3 orbs without recasting it or using recovery options. If you don't, an extra Head Hunt cast is required at the end of Cycle 2.
  2. Using Head Hunt in Cycle 2 may force you to cast it at the end of the next Cycle 1, which creates downtime.
  3. Maelstrom management is extremely important when the rotation fails: cast it as it expires if needed.

Opener from 0-2 orbs

  1. Cycle 1 if Deathly Slash is available, otherwise start from Maelstrom + Cycle 2.

Recovery

  1. Watch this lengthy 111 (Head Hunt) recovery video guide or consider an easier build.
  2. Use spare Twin Shadows/Maelstrom stacks and/or Blitz Rush if you miss major skills.

docs.title: 313 (High Floor) 💜
docs.text:
Best For: Players who want a simpler, faster, and more forgiving Fatal Wave build.

Tradeoff: Lower damage ceiling, but easier to recover from mistakes.

  • Head Hunt is always free for counters, recovery, purify, or Adrenaline upkeep.
  • Accessible from a 14p Star core as 113 (Arts), a transitional core-limited option.
  • Move on to 333 (Ceiling) when you're ready, or stay here if you prefer!

docs.title: Rotation
docs.text:
Use an opener (optional), then alternate between Cycle 1 and Cycle 2 as needed for the rest of the encounter.

The opener stacks Adrenaline and applies synergies efficiently. If it feels overwhelming, just apply synergy and Surge.

Opener from 3 orbs (Stimulant)

  1. If available, Blade Assault is interchangeable with Cycle 2.
  2. It's efficient to use Atropine after Deathly Slash, with Blade Assault available.

Alternating cycles

1Void Strike + Deathly Slash Cycle 2Soul Absorber + Blitz Rush Cycle
  1. Aim to fit up to Cycle 2's Twin Shadows under Cycle 1's Maelstrom to reach 3 orbs without recasting it or using recovery options. If you only landed up to Soul Absorber, an extra Head Hunt cast is usually enough.
  2. The Maelstrom in Cycle 2 is only cast if you'd otherwise miss 3 orbs. Use your judgment. If cast, it lasts at least until Cycle 1's Void Strike; recasting it as it expires aligns cooldowns. If it wasn't needed or it didn't last, nothing changes.

Opener from 0-2 orbs

  1. Cycle 1 if Deathly Slash is available, otherwise start from Maelstrom + Cycle 2.
  2. Prioritize Turning Slash earlier for synergy and Deathly Slash last for Adrenaline/RE buff.

Recovery

  1. Watch this 2-minute 333 recovery video and read the segment titles.
    • 313 plays very similarly, just Turning Slash → Fatal Wave instead of FTF.
  2. Use Head Hunt whenever you're a little short on orbs. Just cast it if unsure.
  3. Use spare Twin Shadows/Maelstrom stacks and/or Blitz Rush if you miss major skills.
  4. Use Head Hunt instead of Twin Shadows for a cycle to recover its stacks if needed.
  5. Use Maelstrom + Fatal Wave earlier if you're waiting on main orb generation skills.

docs.title: 333 (Ceiling) ✨
docs.text:
Best For: Players who want the highest damage RE build.

Tradeoff: Slightly lower orb generation and a less forgiving rotation.

  • Uses Fatal Wave as two fast casts (FTF combo) via a skill reset.
  • Head Hunt is always free for counters, recovery, purify, or Adrenaline upkeep.
  • High gem efficiency: Fatal Wave and Deathly Slash are most of your DPS.
  • Susceptible to high ping or low FPS, but you can compensate with a few changes.

docs.title: Calculator Guide
docs.text: This page explains what the Ark Passive Calculator works out, what it assumes, and why. Each section starts in plain terms. Where there is a formula, a collapsed The math block holds it with worked examples, so you can check any number yourself. Examples use the default inputs on the RE 333 build unless stated.

docs.title: The short version
docs.text:
• Everything is a ratio against your current setup. "% of best" and "gain" compare one choice with another while everything else stays equal. The calculator does not predict absolute DPS or simulate a rotation. It models your damage chain: crit, Crit Damage, Evolution Damage, Additional Damage and Attack Power.
  • Top Combinations scores nine Evolution setups against your stats and shows the best five. Gaps under 0.5 percentage points are a tie, so pick whichever is easier to play.
  • Bonuses that are only on part of the time (Adrenaline, Back Attack, Flash Orb, Maelstrom) are not averaged before the crit cap. Each on/off combination is capped first, then weighted by how likely it is.
  • A Support is assumed by default, a generic above-average one. Lines that raise only your own Weapon Power or Main Stat are worth less because of it. Percent Attack Power is not diluted.
  • Comparisons re-pick your best keystones for each option, so a bracelet gets credit for a keystone change it makes possible. This "realized gain" is never lower than the gain with keystones held fixed.
  • Defaults are typical values from combat logs. Change them to your own. Everything here is a best-effort estimate from tooltips, in-game tests and logs, not a measurement of your character.

docs.title: Top Combinations
docs.text:
The Evolution tree lets you take two of the three Tier 4 keystones (Critical, Master, Pulverize) and split your Limit Break and Keen Sense points. That makes nine setups. The calculator scores all nine against your stats and lists the best five, each as a percentage of the best. Clicking a tab previews a lower-ranked setup. The pin button makes every panel below use it, which is how you test a setup you prefer.

Close results are a tie. Gaps under 0.5 percentage points of DPS do not matter in practice, so choose what is easier to play or what you already have. The 0.5 is a rule of thumb, not a measured error bar: the model uses one blended crit rate for the whole fight and cannot resolve much smaller differences.

Rank Setup % of best 1 LB1/KS2, Master + Pulverize 100.00% 2 LB2/KS1, Master + Pulverize 99.81% 3 LB1/KS2, Critical + Pulverize 99.66% 4 LB3, Master + Pulverize 99.47% 5 LB1/KS2, Critical + Master 99.35%

With the best setup your effective crit rate reads 92.37% (77.37% before the picks), Evolution Damage 81.00% (41.00% before) and Additional Damage 46.86% (38.36% before).

MathThe math

Each of the nine cells gets a score:

score = ((1 - c) + c * CritDmg * (1 + onCrit)) * (1 + evo) * (1 + add)

then times 0.98 if Keen Blunt Weapon is equipped. "% of best" is a cell's score divided by the best score.

  • c is your effective crit rate, capped at 100% (how it is averaged is in the next section).
  • CritDmg is your Crit Damage: base 2.0 plus rings, bracelet, Keen Blunt Weapon, the Swift core and others.
  • onCrit is the extra damage on crit hits (Crit Hit Damage Synergy and similar). Critical multiplies it by 1.12.
  • evo is Evolution Damage. Pulverize adds 20 points to it.
  • add is Additional Damage. Master adds 8.5 points to it.
  • Master also adds 7% crit rate. That shares the 100% cap, so Master is worth less as your crit rate nears the cap.

Keen Blunt Weapon's downside is an expected value, a 10% chance of -20% damage, so a flat x0.98. Optimized Training 1 takes one of the three keystone points, so with it ticked the splits become OT1/LB2, OT1/LB1/KS1 and OT1/KS2 (there is no LB3), and it adds its own 5 points of Evolution Damage. Its cooldown reduction is not counted, so at the defaults it reads -2.8% DPS: the best split with it against the best without it.

LimitsAssumptions and limits

One blended crit rate and one multiplier chain for the whole fight, so skill-by-skill differences are not modeled.

docs.title: Uptimes and estimated inputs
docs.text:
Many bonuses are only on part of the time. The calculator does not just add "bonus times uptime" to your crit rate. Crit rate is capped at 100%, and averaging before the cap overstates what you get near it. So it works out every on/off combination first, caps each one, and only then averages.

Two inputs are worth knowing exactly. Adrenaline uptime is the share of damage dealt at 6 stacks, which is what a DPS meter reports. Its Crit Rate bonus needs all 6 stacks, so it scales with that uptime, while its Attack Power bonus works per stack and gets partial credit as stacks rebuild. Back Attack Rate is the figure from the Combat Analyzer's Overview tab. It counts hits, not damage, and only for skills that can back attack.

MathThe math

Crit rate. Three independent sometimes-on terms: Adrenaline (bonus times uptime), Back Attack (10% times your effective back attack share) and Flash Orb (bonus times uptime). blendCritTerms takes every on/off combination, caps each at 100% and weights it by its joint probability. Averaging first is wrong because the cap is concave.

Example (Flash Orb left out for simplicity): base crit 75%, Adrenaline +20% at 97% uptime, Back Attack +10% at 90%. Averaging first gives 75% + 19.4% + 9% = 103.4%, capped to 100.000%. The joint-probability method gives 99.035%:

Adrenaline Back Attack Probability Crit rate on on 87.3% 105% capped to 100% on off 9.7% 95% off on 2.7% 85% off off 0.3% 75%

Weighted: 0.873 + 0.09215 + 0.02295 + 0.00225 = 0.99035. Raid Captain's Move Speed works the same way.

Adrenaline. Outside 6 stacks you rebuild one stack per cast, so the first five casts average 3 of 6 stacks, or 0.5. The AP half of the bonus uses that:

AP from Adrenaline = full * (U + (1 - U) * 0.5)
full = 6 stacks * (0.9% + stone bonus per stack)

At the defaults (4 nodes, no stone) the full value is 5.4% Attack Power:

Uptime Adrenaline AP Adrenaline crit Effective crit rate (before picks) Final Attack Power 100% 5.40% 20.0% 77.98% 346,412 97% 5.32% 19.4% 77.37% 346,161 80% 4.86% 16.0% 73.98% 344,741 50% 4.05% 10.0% 67.98% 342,233

Back Attack. The rate is used as the damage share of the skills that can back attack, which holds when their hits are similar in size. On Surge builds the share is 0.95 times the rate. On RE builds the skills that always land as back attacks (Surge, which also scales with Specialization) take their own share, your rate gates the rest, with no double counting.

The 0.5 rebuild share is a derivation, not a measurement. Later skills hit harder and would push it up slightly, by about 0.1 Attack Power points at 80% uptime. The Adrenaline input has no floor: low values are fair what-ifs, but an uptime of 0 still reports half the AP bonus, which cannot happen in a fight.

LimitsAssumptions and limits

The terms are treated as independent. In practice they are usually on together, since you aim to back attack constantly and keep your stacks, while Flash Orb is RNG with low uptime. At high uptimes this does little harm.

docs.title: Build, presets and loading a character
docs.text:
The Build toggle. The five builds (RE 111/313, RE 333, Surge 111, Surge 222, Surge 333) change the following:

  • Spec share. The Spec row and the Bracelet vs Bracelet Spec input use the Surge skill's share of that build's damage, read from the build pages' Trixion charts. Awakening is 1.5% of damage on RE and 1% on Surge.
  • Back attack. On RE, Surge always lands as a back attack, so its chart share is the always-back-attack share and the Back Attack rate covers only the rest. On Surge builds the share is 0.95 times the rate.
  • Maelstrom uptime default. 85% on RE, 80% on Surge 111 and 333, 90% on Surge 222. It is reset when you switch between groups (RE, Surge 111/333, Surge 222) and left alone inside a group, so a value you typed survives.
  • Food and runes. Mana Food, Vernese Wine, Mass Increase and the Rage Rune only apply where the build uses them. On RE, Mana Food is informational and left out of the DPS totals.
  • Breaking Moon. Surge 111 only: its average Crit Damage is added.
  • Move Speed. The class passive is 12 on RE and 10 on Surge.

The Order Core table does not follow the toggle. Each core is judged on the build it belongs to.

Presets. There are three slots. Every change is saved to the active slot in your browser, and switching slots loads that slot. Reset clears only the active slot, after a confirmation.

Export and Import. Export writes the active slot as text. Import first resets every field to its default, then applies what the text contains, so a field missing from the text ends up at its default and not at your previous value. Options the calculator does not recognise are skipped and listed. The Setup A vs B, Bracelet A vs B and Ability Stone sandbox fields are not part of an export and always start fresh.

Load Character. Enter a character name or a Bible link. The calculator reads the raid loadout from that character's lostark.bible page and runs it through the same Import path. When it can tell from the Order cores, it also sets the Build for you. Some rules decide what gets loaded and how much to trust it:

  • It uses the character's most recent raid loadout. The Chaos Dungeon loadout is never used.
  • If that raid loadout has no gems, or there is none, it falls back to Bible's estimated raid loadout and says so. That is the best raid gear Bible has seen, which can differ from what the character wears now.
  • Anything it could not read (an unknown tier, an unreadable core grade, a Build it could not match) is listed as a warning and left at its default, so check the list before trusting the numbers.
  • It refuses characters that are not Deathblades.

docs.title: Support
docs.text:
Most raid parties have a Support, and a Support raises your Attack Power. A calculator that ignored this would overvalue upgrades that only raise your own Weapon Power or Main Stat, because the Support's share does not grow with them. So Support is on by default, modeled as a generic one: above average, not maxed, with the same Weapon Power, Main Stat and kind of Ability Stone as you, and the gearing a Support like that would likely have.

When you compare "what if I had this line", the Support stays at its current value, because the line is yours and not your Support's. Lines that raise only your own Weapon Power, Main Stat or flat Attack Power are diluted that way. Percent Attack Power is not. This is the low end of a range: the real answer for your party sits between the number shown and the case where your Support gears up alongside you.

MathThe math 
AP = floor( ( sqrt(WP * MainStat / 6) * BaseAP + FlatAP + SupportBuff ) * PercentAP )
SupportBuff = sqrt(WP * MainStat / 6) * BaseAP * 0.4 * (SupportUptime / 100)

The buff sits inside the bracket, so Percent AP multiplies it too. The 0.4 comes from the reference spreadsheet's Support profile, which has specific gearing. That profile is what is modeled, so the Support bracelet's own "Ally Atk. Power Enhancement" line is not modeled separately.

At the defaults (98% uptime) the Support adds about 39% to your Attack Power: the final readout is 249,529 without it and 346,161 with it, a difference of 96,632. The Support's own term inside the bracket is 86,411, and Percent AP multiplies it like everything else, which is why the final difference is larger. The checkbox also turns on the +14% Evolution Damage that goes with having a Support and the Support's Move Speed bonus (its Attack Speed bonus is not scored), so switching it off changes more than Attack Power. At the defaults it also moves LB2/KS1 Master + Pulverize to first.

Why some gains are diluted and others are not. A Weapon Power line acts on only your part of the bracket, while Percent Attack Power multiplies all of it, Support included. From the bracelet table at the defaults:

Bracelet line With Support Without Support Weapon Power +7200 1.05% 1.45% Weapon Power +9000 1.31% 1.81% Attack Power +0.4% (percent) 0.37% 0.37%

The Weapon Power rows keep about 72% of their no-Support value, which is 1 / (1 + 0.4 * 0.98). If the Support gears up alongside you, nothing is diluted. The Attack Power readout shows that end of the range: +5% Weapon Power there, with the Support following your stats, gives +2.45% with a Support and +2.44% without.

Orbs. Flash Orb and Strength Orb use an Ether effectiveness of 0.31, from a maxed relic Drops of Ether engraving (16%) plus a Level 2 stone (15%). Flash Orb adds 15% crit rate and Strength Orb adds 10% Attack Power, each times 1.31.

LimitsAssumptions and limits

The 0.4 coefficient and the generic gearing are one reference profile. A much better or worse Support shifts every Weapon Power, Main Stat, flat AP and Base AP row by roughly the same factor.

docs.title: Why every comparison is re-optimized
docs.text:
Say you compare two bracelets. A bracelet changes your crit rate, Crit Damage or Additional Damage, and those decide which of the nine keystone setups is best. So the honest question is not "how much better is the new bracelet if I keep my keystones" but "how much better is my best setup with it than my best setup without it". That is what the calculator reports, and it calls it the realized gain.

MathThe math

For each candidate it finds the best of the nine cells with the candidate and for your current setup, then divides:

realized gain = best(candidate) / best(current) - 1
fixed gain    = candidate in current best cell / best(current) - 1

The realized gain is never below the fixed gain. Your current best cell is one of the candidate's options, so the candidate's best is at least as good, and both gains share the same denominator. A check on 4,000 random input sets found no violations. The gap can be real: the largest seen was 3.2 percentage points of DPS. With a pin, both sides use the pinned cell and the two gains are equal.

The best cell flips in cases like Keen Blunt Weapon at the defaults (with it Master + Pulverize at LB1/KS2, without it Critical + Pulverize at LB1/KS2), the Chaos Core Flashy comparison (228 flips in about 180,000 synthetic gear profiles), and bracelet lines such as High Crit Rate or High Additional Damage.

Bracelet vs Bracelet re-optimizes every line that feeds the nine cells: Crit Rate, Crit Damage, Crit Stat and Additional Damage. Back Attack, Outgoing, Stagger and Damage plus Cooldown lines, and the vs Demon/Archdemon half of an Additional Damage line, multiply every cell by the same factor, so they cannot change the winner.

LimitsAssumptions and limits

Realized gain is the gain for a player who re-picks keystones, not a measurement of the gain with fixed ones.

docs.title: Reference: how each panel is valued
docs.text: The sections below cover how individual parts of the calculator are valued. Skip to the one you are checking.

docs.title: Attack Power
docs.text:
Attack Power comes from your Weapon Power and Main Stat, scaled by the Base Attack Power % from your gems, plus any flat Attack Power and the Support's buff, all multiplied by your Attack Power %. The readout in the Weapon Power / Main Stat card shows three stages so you can hold it against your character sheet.

Stage Value What is in it Base 237,661 What the Character Profile shows in a town: no Adrenaline, no Support, no raid buffs With Adrenaline 249,710 Adds Adrenaline at all 6 stacks (5.40%) Final 346,161 Adrenaline at your uptime (5.32%), the Support, plus Atropine, Strength Orb and others if set

The final value is the baseline every Attack Power based comparison uses.

MathThe math

The formula is the one in the Support section. Its pieces:

  • BaseAP is 1 plus your gem Base AP % (summed over every gem, so eleven Lv. 10 gems at 1.2% each is 13.2%), plus 1.5% when your Ability Stone's two engraving levels add up to 5 or more (9/7 and 10/6 nodes are the smallest that do).
  • FlatAP is your flat Attack Power plus the flat half of Chaos Core: Attack.
  • PercentAP is 1 plus: both Attack Power earrings, Kazeros (2%), Guardian (3%), the Attack % half of Chaos Core: Attack, Astrogem Attack Power, the Attack Power % Other field, Atropine (30% times its uptime), Strength Orb (10% times 1.31 times its uptime) and the Adrenaline model.
  • Astrogem Attack Power is level / 120 x 4.4%, rounded down to two decimals as the game shows it (level 35: 1.28%).
  • The whole bracket, including the final multiply, sits inside the floor.

Worked example. Weapon Power 259,216, Main Stat 854,918, gem Base AP 13.2% plus the 1.5% stone bonus, Chaos Core: Attack at Relic 20 points (+2.13% and 2,700 flat). The square root part is 192,184, times 1.147 is 220,435. Attack Power % is 3.10 (two High earrings) + 2.13 (Chaos Core) + 1.28 (Astrogem) = 6.51, plus Adrenaline. Base is floor((220,435 + 2,700) x 1.0651) = 237,661. Final has the Support's 86,411 inside the bracket, about +96,632 after Percent AP. The first two stages leave out Atropine, Strength Orb and Attack Power % Other so they match the Character Profile.

LimitsAssumptions and limits

Weapon Power and Main Stat are not rebuilt from gear, so a wrong entry shifts every row that uses them.

docs.title: Crit and damage layers
docs.text:
Your damage is four layers that multiply: crit rate and Crit Damage, the extra damage on crit hits (Crit Hit Damage), Evolution Damage, and Additional Damage. Each layer is its own multiplier, so a point added to a small layer is worth more than a point added to a big one. Every row on this page changes one of them.

Each keystone changes one layer: Critical boosts the extra damage on crit hits, Master adds crit rate and Additional Damage, and Pulverize adds Evolution Damage. The summary card shows two crit figures. Eff. Crit Rate is the capped, probability-weighted value the score uses. Peak Crit Rate adds every bonus at full strength with no cap, can read above 100%, and only shows the ceiling in a burst window.

MathThe math

The sources of each layer, with the RE 333 default value:

Layer How sources combine Default build Crit rate Added, then capped at 100% with the uptime blend Crit stat 658 gives 23.55% (stat x 0.03579099 / 100 as a fraction, 0.2355 after rounding down to 4 decimals), rings 1.90, bracelet 4.20, Adrenaline 19.40, strike 20, Back Attack 8.32, total 77.37% Crit Damage Added to the base 200% Rings 8, bracelet 6.8, Keen Blunt Weapon 52, strike 32, total 298.80% Crit Hit Damage Each source multiplies the others Two bracelet lines at 1.5% and Chaos Core: Flashy Ancient 17P at 1.65% give 1.015 x 1.015 x 1.0165, which is +4.72% Evolution Damage Added Yearning 14, Evolution Karma rank 6 gives 6, Standing Striker 21, total 41% Additional Damage Added Pet 1.0, weapon quality 30, necklace 2.6, Astrogem 4.76, total 38.36%

Other sources: Keen Sense adds Crit Rate (4% per level) and Evolution Damage (5% per level). Limit Break adds 10% Evolution Damage per level. Crit Rate synergies add 10% each, two Crit Hit Damage synergies multiply by 1.08 each, and Optimized Training 1 adds 5% Evolution Damage. Weapon quality adds 10% plus 0.002% times quality squared (quality 100 gives 30%). Astrogem Additional Damage is the level times 8.0834, rounded down, over 10,000 (level 59 gives 4.76%). Keen Blunt Weapon adds 44% to 52% Crit Damage by node and its stone adds 7.5% to 15%.

Check for the best cell at the defaults (LB1/KS2, Master + Pulverize): effective crit 92.37%, Crit Damage 2.988, Crit Hit Damage 1.0472, Evolution 1 + 0.81, Additional 1 + 0.4686.

((1 - 0.9238) + 0.9238 * 2.988 * 1.0472) * 1.81 * 1.4686 * 0.98 = 7.73

Only ratios of this number are ever shown, so the absolute value means nothing alone. Doing all nine cells this way by hand gives the same five percentages as the Top Combinations table.

Crit Rate Dual and Crit Damage Dual are the bracelet lines that carry a 1.5% Crit Hit Damage bonus.

LimitsAssumptions and limits

Which sources multiply and which add follows the game's tooltips and in-game tests. A source in a different layer would change its own value, not the rest of the chain. Breaking Moon is folded into Crit Damage as an average per cast.

docs.title: Ark Grid cores
docs.text:
The Ark Grid Core Comparison answers one question per core: how much more DPS this core gives than an empty slot. A grid holds one Sun core (Flashy, Stable, Swift), one Moon core (Smoldering, Absorbing, Crushing) and one Star core (Attack, Weapon), so each row removes only your current core in its own slot and keeps the other two.

Chaos Core, 20 points Relic Ancient Relic to Ancient Flashy Attack 3.09% 4.14% +1.03% Smoldering Strike 2.60% 3.78% +1.14% Attack 2.84% 3.64% +0.78% Absorbing Strike 1.99% 3.00% +0.99% Stable Attack 1.90% 2.85% +0.94% Crushing Strike 1.85% 2.78% +0.92% Swift Attack 1.81% 2.72% +0.90% Weapon 1.55% 1.98% +0.43%

For Order cores, only their 17 point line differs between Relic and Ancient, so that line is the whole comparison.

MathThe math

Chaos Core effects unlock at 10, 14, 17, 18, 19 and 20 points. The tables hold the cumulative totals at each level from in-game tooltips and tests. Relic and Ancient are identical below 17 points. Every gain is DPS with the core divided by DPS without it, minus 1, and the last column is

upgrade = (1 + Ancient 20P gain) / (1 + Relic 20P gain) - 1

By kind of row:

  • Crit Hit Damage (Flashy), Crit Damage (Swift), Crit Rate (Crushing) and Additional Damage (Stable) feed the grid, so both sides use the nine cell search.
  • Damage to foes lines (Flashy's Damage %, Smoldering's Boss Damage, Absorbing's Damage) multiply instead of adding. A core's 14, 17 and 18 to 20 point lines combine as (1 + a)(1 + b)(1.0016)^n - 1, about 0.01 to 0.02 points above the plain sum of the tooltip figures.
  • Smoldering's Burn half does not depend on points. It is 0.6% of total damage at Relic and 1.25 times that at Ancient, and it multiplies with the Boss Damage half.
  • Chaos Core: Attack and Weapon use the Attack Power formula with the Support held fixed. Attack and Weapon share the Star slot, so whichever Star core you wear is removed first: the Attack core's lines drop out of Attack Power, and the Weapon core's share is divided back out of your typed Weapon Power. Sun and Moon cores do not affect these rows. The Support stays at the value for your real typed Weapon Power. Weapon is folded into your typed Weapon Power: the new value is WP * (1 + (pct / 100) / WPmult) + flat * WPmult, where pct is the core's Weapon Power % in points and WPmult is your Weapon Power multiplier (1 + total Weapon Power % / 100).
  • Not modeled: Speed, Stable's damage reduction, Swift's Attack Speed, Absorbing's healing and the non-damage half of Crushing (a weak point utility buff with no DPS value). Crushing's Crit Rate half is valued.

At the defaults, Ancient 20 points: Smoldering is (1 + 3.0028%) x (1 + 0.75%) - 1 = 3.78%, Absorbing is simply 3.00%, and Chaos Core: Weapon turns 259,216 Weapon Power into 273,732 (+5.6%) for a 1.98% gain after the fixed Support dilutes it. Swift's +8.35% Crit Damage reads 2.72%, which a hand computation of the nine cells with and without it also gives.

Order cores. With s the share of your damage the line touches, r the Relic bonus and a the Ancient bonus:

relic total = 1 - s + s * (1 + r) / (1 + a)
gain = 1 / relic total - 1

The shares are measured with the core already Ancient (they come from the build pages' Trixion damage charts), so the Relic total is the Ancient one with the extra bonus divided back out. A Damage to foes line touches everything (s = 1). A Normal Skill Damage line touches everything except Surge and Awakening, a proxy that leaves a small amount of bleed and other non-skill damage in the share.

  • Swift Resolution (222) hits Deathly Slash (35.5% of damage), 15% vs 20%: 1 / (0.645 + 0.355 x 1.15 / 1.20) - 1 = 1.50%.
  • Arts Core on RE 111 touches 78.6% of damage (100% minus Surge 19.9% minus Awakening 1.5%) at +5% vs +6%: 0.75%.
  • Some cores carry a stack count or a coverage below 100%, which the table's detail line states.

The shares are the build pages' measured chart values, and a script keeps the calculator's copy in step with them.

LimitsAssumptions and limits

Each Order core is judged on one build, the one it is used on, so that table is not a ranking across builds. Smoldering's Burn estimate and the grade tables are the assumptions to watch.

docs.title: Bracelet, Accessory and A vs B comparisons
docs.text:
These panels value one line or one whole piece at a time, always as a ratio to a baseline. The Bracelet and Accessory tables answer "what is this line worth". The two A vs B panels are sandboxes: enter your equipped piece as A and a candidate replacement as B, and see which is better.

MathThe math

Bracelet Line Comparison. The crit, damage and Additional Damage rows are valued against your setup with your own bracelet removed: bracelet lines off, both Dual checkboxes off, and your Crit Stat reset to a bracelet-free 576 (a character with all side content done, used only so your current bracelet is not counted twice). One candidate line is added, the nine cell search runs for both sides, and the result is the ratio. The Weapon Power and Main Stat rows work differently, as the list below says. By kind of row:

  • Crit Rate, Crit Damage, Crit Stat and Additional Damage lines go through the full search.
  • Back Attack Damage is the tabled value times the 0.95 back attack share (2.5% reads 2.38%). Outgoing Damage plus Damage to Staggered adds the Stagger line at the 5% share (2% + 4% x 0.05 reads 2.20%). Damage plus Cooldown reads the damage value minus 1 point as an estimate for the cooldown half (4.5% reads 3.50%).
  • Weapon Power, Main Stat and Attack Power lines use the Attack Power formula with the Support fixed, so a Weapon Power line reads about 72% of its no-Support value. They are added on top of the Weapon Power and Main Stat you typed, and there is no field for your equipped bracelet's own line to remove, so a Weapon Power or Main Stat line already on your bracelet stays in the baseline (Bracelet vs Bracelet does remove it: side A is your worn bracelet). At the defaults, with an equipped Mid line (8,100 Weapon Power or 14,000 Main Stat), the Weapon Power rows read about 0.03 to 0.05 points low and the Main Stat rows about 0.01 points low. Both are well inside the 0.5 point tie band.
  • Spec Stat has its own model. The gain per point is (m - 1) / (1735 * m) where m = 1 + (0.86 * shareRatio + 0.1528 * awakeningRatio) / 699 * 1735. The two ratios say how much of your damage comes from the skill Spec scales and from your Awakening, each normalized at a reference Spec of 1855. On RE 333 (16.6% skill share, 1.5% Awakening) +100 Spec reads 0.65%. It counts damage only, not cooldown reduction.
  • A few Weapon Power lines use an assumed stack count, fight length or uptime, listed in the register.

Check: High Crit Rate +5% with its +1.5% Crit Hit Damage bonus reads 5.18% in the table and in a hand computation.

Accessory Line Comparison. Same idea, but each table clears only the piece it lists and keeps the rest of your gear. Necklace clears your necklace line, Rings clears both rings' Crit lines, and Earrings clears both earrings' Attack Power % and Weapon Power % lines, so each candidate is valued as the only line on that slot. The lines that can roll on any accessory (flat Weapon Power, flat Attack Power and Quality STR/DEX/INT) clear nothing and are added on top of your full gear, so a line of that kind already on one of your pieces stays in the baseline; Accessory vs Accessory is the tool for swapping one. Necklace, earring and ring tables also show the two lines of one piece rolled together (LL, ML, MM, HL, HM, HH, for Low, Mid and High). Earrings are the one case where a line feeds Weapon Power %, so your base Weapon Power is reverse-derived from the total you typed and your Weapon Power % fields, and is only as exact as those fields.

Bracelet vs Bracelet and Accessory vs Accessory. Each side is valued as four layers: the keystone, crit and Additional Damage lines (searched), Spec, the flat lines, and Attack Power plus Weapon Power. Each layer is computed alone against the same baseline, and the layers are multiplied. The default bracelet reads +14.71%, about 1.1397 x 1.0065 x 1.0000 x 1.0000 (its lines are Crit Rate, Crit Damage and Additional Damage, so the flat layer is empty). Damage plus Cooldown uses the raw tag in the sandbox unless you tick the box, because the cooldown value is personal. Side A is always treated as your equipped piece, and any Main Stat or flat Weapon Power line on it is backed out of the shared baseline (Bracelet vs Bracelet backs out only its Weapon Power and Main Stat lines, since the other layers already start from a bracelet-free baseline). Main Stat counts with your Main Stat %, and flat Weapon Power with your Weapon Power %, on both sides. The reference table applies the Damage plus Cooldown penalty by default.

LimitsAssumptions and limits

Layers are treated as independent, so an interaction between, say, Spec and Attack Power is ignored. The Bracelet Weapon Power and Main Stat rows and the Any Accessory Slot rows sit on top of your typed totals, so a line of the same kind already on your gear stays in the baseline. The A vs B panels remove side A's lines instead.

docs.title: Engravings and Raid Captain
docs.text:
The Engraving Comparison shows what each engraving is worth and which two flexible engravings work best together. Raid Captain depends on Move Speed, so its value follows a Move Speed estimate. That estimate uses the same expand-then-cap method as the crit rate, so a high average does not hide the time spent below the cap.

MathThe math
  • Grudge, Cursed Doll and Mass Increase are tabled values by node level, plus your Ability Stone level. Grudge at 4 nodes reads 21.00% and Cursed Doll 17.00%.
  • Ambush Master is two multiplying parts: the Back Attack Damage half (15% times your effective back attack share, 0.832 at the defaults) and the book-level Damage half (7.6% at 4 nodes). That is 1.12486 x 1.076 - 1 = 21.03%.
  • Adrenaline and Keen Blunt Weapon use a real with-and-without search, so the winning keystone can flip, as in the Ark Grid rows. The Keen Blunt Weapon stone-level preview works the same way.
  • Raid Captain's tabled value (48% at 4 nodes) is its bonus per 100 points of Move Speed above 100%. Move Speed is capped at 140%, so the cap pays 40% of the tabled value (19.2% at 4 nodes). The row is the node value times (expected capped Move Speed minus 100) over 100.
  • The Ability Stone's Base AP row is your Attack Power with and without the stone's +1.5% Base AP, with the Support's buff the same on both sides (it is assumed to carry the same kind of stone as you). The +1.5% adds to your gem Base AP, so the gain is below 1.5%, and the Support's share of Attack Power lowers it further: at the defaults the row reads 0.94% with the Support and 1.31% with none. It applies when the two stone levels add up to 5 or more.
  • Mana Food's row is the Main Stat gain through the Attack Power formula, Support fixed. On Surge 111 and 333 it also carries the Maelstrom Bleed rune's +0.75% damage. On RE it is informational and left out of every DPS total.
  • Best Combo and Runner-Up search every pair of the flexible engravings (Raid Captain, Keen Blunt Weapon, Cursed Doll, plus Mass Increase on Surge if you opt in), valued together. Raid Captain is in the pool on both specs so you can see its value even if you would not drop it. At the defaults the best pair is Raid Captain plus Keen Blunt Weapon at +39.42%, 0.74% ahead of Raid Captain plus Cursed Doll at +38.40%. The 0.74% compares the two whole setups (1.3942 / 1.3840 - 1), so it is not the 1.02 point difference between the displayed gains.
  • Setup A vs Setup B compares two whole loadouts of your choice the same way, with your food held fixed. On Surge that can mislead, because Wine only helps a setup that has Raid Captain. Overall Best therefore lets each setup pick its better food (Wine, or Mana Food with its Main Stat and Bleed gain) before comparing the two. Best Combo has the same note for the best pair under each food. RE has no second food choice, so neither note appears there.

Move Speed. Every on/off combination of the sometimes-on sources is capped at 140% and weighted by its joint probability. At the RE 333 defaults the base is 127.32% (106.32 base, 12 class passive, 9 Passionate Dance) and Maelstrom adds 12.8% at 85% uptime. The expected capped Move Speed is 138.10%, shown as Raid Captain Efficiency 95.25% (the share of the way from 100% to the 140% cap). Capping the average instead would read 95.50%. With the Paladin checkbox added (24.6% at a 35% assumed uptime) the true figure is 96.91%, while capping the average would read 100.00% and hide that you are still below the cap part of the time. The Raid Captain row in the engraving table is its node value times the Move Speed above 100% as a fraction, (138.10 - 100) / 100 = 0.38098. That is the 95.25% efficiency times the 0.40 the cap allows. So 0.48 (4 nodes, no stone) times 0.38098 gives 18.29%.

Sources: base 106.32, plus 12 from the class on RE (10 on Surge), Passionate Dance 9 with a Support, Valkyrie or Artist 8, and Vernese Wine 3 on Surge when you do not use Mana Food. The 8 is exactly Valkyrie's Move Speed at 100% uptime. Artist (a skill-based 10% at 70-100% uptime) is grouped in for simplicity, so no uptime or skill input is needed. Maelstrom (12.8), Rage Rune (16 on Surge) and Paladin (24.6) are sometimes-on, at the register's uptimes. The cap is 140.

Mass Increase's Attack Speed drawback is not modeled, which is why it is an opt-in checkbox. Attack Speed is not tracked at all, because nothing on this page depends on it.

Ability Stone penalties are not tracked. Attack Power Reduction (2%, 4% or 6% in game) subtracts from your other Attack Power % sources, such as Adrenaline or the Kazeros astrogems, so it would lower every Attack Power based row. Move Speed Reduction (also 2%, 4% or 6%) subtracts from Move Speed, which Raid Captain reads.

LimitsAssumptions and limits

Move Speed sources are treated as independent. Ability Stone penalties and Attack Speed are not tracked.

docs.title: Known limits and how to challenge it
docs.text:
Not modeled: skill-by-skill crit differences, rotation effects, Optimized Training 1's cooldown reduction, each Chaos Core's non-damage half (Speed, damage reduction, healing and Crushing's weak point utility buff), Mass Increase's Attack Speed drawback, Attack Speed in general and Ability Stone penalties.

What would improve it: your own measured values. Every default can be changed, and the Combat Analyzer figures (Adrenaline coverage, Back Attack Rate, Raid Captain Efficiency) are the most useful ones to replace. If you think a rule is wrong, report the section, the input values you used and the number you expected.

How it was checked: tooltips and in-game tests for Ark Grid and engraving values, combat logs for the estimated rates, and the reference spreadsheets (1, 2) for formula structure. Credit to their authors: this calculator started from that work and has since moved well beyond it for this class, so the sheets are no longer a current reference.

TipArk Passive

NoteArk Grid
  • You can level Ark Grid cores to your preference, but 17p Surge Core grants a second Earth Cleaver stack. This frees up a gem slot and allows you to cast Earth Cleaver without needing to hold it for an upcoming raid mechanic.

docs.title: Skill Setup
docs.text:
TipRunes
  • Use Purify on Spincutter if needed.
  • Focus on Maelstrom + wine handles most mana needs, since Breaking Moon cycles restore it.
    • Use mana food instead if you don't trust your or your support's uptime (spec bards), or for Trixion-like content.
  • Alternatively, Legendary Bleed on Maelstrom + mana food: higher ceiling/lower floor, even with Raid Captain.
NoteOptions & Tripods
  • You can use the Weak Point Detection tripod on Blade Dance.
    • Requires Lv 10 CD gem and/or raid downtime for it not to become a bottleneck.
    • You must swap Wind Cut DMG gem to Blade Dance CD, and it's a marginal DPS increase.
  • Leap Attack vs Earth Explosion tripod on Earth Cleaver is up to personal preference.
    • Earth Explosion is faster and may raise rotation consistency with an extra stack.
    • Leap Attack is slower but increases overall DPS by ~1% and offers more mobility.
  • Dark Axel (1-1-2) can be used instead of Spincutter, but offers no recovery.

docs.title: Gems

    • Mass Increase and/or Optimized Training 1 help smooth things out at low investment levels.
    • +CD% bracelet increases CD gem Lv requirements by 1, and low Specialization makes it worse.

docs.title: Rotation
docs.text:
There's an optimal skill order, but you have flexibility when facing downtime or weaving in mobility skills.

Breaking Moon grants 60 stacks on hit and empowers your next Surge with +60% Critical Damage.

Spincutter is your mobility skill and backup stack builder. Use it to guarantee a back attack on Surge.

Use the Breaking Moon cycle and its follow-up when available, then repeat the regular cycle otherwise.

From 3 orbs

1Breaking Moon Cycle + Follow-Up Alternative · Awakening Follow-Up 2Regular Cycle×2
  1. In the follow-up cycles: cast Maelstrom if you had 2 stacks, otherwise just continue without it.
  2. Do NOT worry about Raid Captain efficiency; Keen Blunt Weapon is just as inefficient or worse!
    • Breaking Moon's Critical Damage bonus to the next Surge (biggest hit) is additive to Keen Blunt Weapon.
    • Raid Captain fully buffs the empowered Surge and can make use of Rage/Atropine for the follow-up.
  3. Blade Assault scales much worse on Surge than on Remaining Energy and takes too long to cast.
    • It's still useful for Atropine openers, or it can be saved to greed with push immunity/Hyper Awakening.
  4. It seems more complicated than it really is, so watch this video to see how a full rotation plays out.
AltStack Reserve Rotation

An alternative to the default rotation. It builds a stack reserve, so you're never short on them. Goes 1>2>2>3>1, etc.

1Breaking Moon Cycle 2Regular Cycle×2 3Pre-Breaking Moon Cycle

From 0 orbs

  1. Use a Stimulant (recommended) or proceed to #2.
    • Rat Pack: Use Maelstrom's Orb Control tripod and Flash Blink awakening.
  2. Generate one orb, build at least 40 stacks, then Surge to refill all 3 orbs.

Atropine usage

  1. Fit three Surges into a 10-second window. Use Atropine right before the first Surge hits.
  2. The second or third Surge must be part of a Breaking Moon cycle or you won't make it.
  3. Stacks and the environment vary, so a fixed rotation would just be a shackle.

docs.title: Skill Setup
docs.text:
TipRunes
  • Use Purify on Head Hunt if needed.
  • Use Focus on Maelstrom if you experience mana issues.
  • Use Legendary Vision on Surprise Attack if you find it more useful than Rage.
    • Increases chance of getting an extra stack on Surprise Attack precast.
    • This is the best and most efficient way to improve stagger contribution.
    • Not recommended with a +CD% bracelet, as you may lose Maelstrom stacks.
NoteOptions & Tripods
  • You can bring Head Hunt down to Lv 1 for lower mana use.
    • Raising it past Lv 4 is not ideal as you lose a stack and increase mana use for little reason.
  • You can use Wide Attack tripod on Surprise Attack for noticeably increased quality of life.
    • With Wide Attack, you must cast Turning Slash early on openers to apply synergy.
    • This is more viable than ever as Turning Slash's lingering hits now extend its uptime.
  • Earth Cleaver can be used instead of Head Hunt if you prefer its mobility or utility.
    • It's a slower, more vulnerable skill cast that consumes significantly more mana.
    • Set Maelstrom and Upper Slash to Lv 10, then raise Earth Cleaver (3-3-1) to Lv 10.
AltDark Axel vs Spincutter

Dark Axel · Default

The build's signature. It recreates RE's Surge using two skills: Dark Axel carries you over the boss, then Deathly Slash precisely slams you into its back.

In the rotation:

  • Usually better CPM when repositioning; faster than 2 or more casts of (tapped) Spincutter.
  • Always cast right before Deathly Slash and Surge, leaving very little to chance.
  • Push immunity panic button that saves your spacebar and lets you greed twice as much.
    • Using it that way limits your mobility for that cycle, but increases uptime on the boss.

Best For: Getting the most out of the build.

Tradeoff: Takes practice, and pays off most once you're used to the advanced skip cycles.

Spincutter (3-3-1) · Alternative

Can replace Dark Axel if you find it more useful on bosses with a small hitbox or Mordum Extreme.

In the rotation:

  • Repositioning with it loses CPM compared to Dark Axel when cast 2 or more times (tapped). A single cast is slightly faster than Dark Axel.
  • Repositioning with it while skipping Upper Slash costs you the free push immune window, one of the build's core benefits. You still have skills left to cast, so you're out of luck if the boss turns.
  • Moves you around the boss, so you aim outward toward its back, risking a miss from Deathly Slash's forward movement.

Best For: Players who prefer simplicity: a single cycle is easier to loop if you don't wish to learn the advanced skip cycles or their recovery options.

Best of both: Swap freely by content, or :ratJAM: run Lv 4 Spincutter instead of Head Hunt when Counter isn't needed.

docs.title: Gems
docs.text:
NoteGem Requirements
  • The gem priority list assumes you will be using a rotation with the advanced skip cycles.
    • Upper Slash and Surprise Attack CDs at Lv 9 are roughly enough, but higher is always better.
    • Once Blade Dance and Maelstrom CDs are at Lv 9, Wind Cut CD overtakes them in priority.
    • Mass Increase and/or Optimized Training 1 help smooth things out at low investment levels.
    • +CD% bracelet increases CD gem Lv requirements by 1, and low Specialization makes it worse.

docs.title: Rotation
docs.text:
There's an optimal skill order, but you have flexibility when facing downtime or weaving in mobility skills.

'Destiny: Enhanced Sharpness' can be stacked up to 5 times by using (Normal) skills to empower Deathly Slash.

Use Dark Axel to guarantee back attacks on Deathly Slash and Surge if needed.

Use the Opener cycle and either loop it forever (easy) or continue on to the advanced skip cycles (ceiling DPS).

From 3 orbs

1Opener/Overstack Cycle - 68 Stacks
  1. This opener chains into the cycles below, but it's fine by itself if you prefer simplicity and don't mind downtime.
  2. On raid openers or after extended downtime, you can use Deathly Slash instead of Wind Cut as a precast.

Leopard Mode (Recommended)

After the opener, alternate between these two cycles as needed for ceiling DPS:

2Surprise Skip Cycle - 61 Stacks 3Wind Cut Skip Cycle - 60 Stacks
  1. Cycle 2 offers safety by leaving Surprise Attack as a recovery option; Cycle 3 offers higher CPM.
  2. Rotating 2>3>2>3 is ideal, but based on boss patterns, variations like 2>3>3>2 or 2>2>3>3 are valid.
    • Cycle 3 is preferred during risky boss patterns because Wind Cut lacks Paralysis Immunity.
    • Recover with Wind Cut or Surprise Attack, and decide your next cycle based on the available one.
  3. You can skip a Surprise Attack finisher whenever you're at 49+ stacks before Deathly Slash.
    • Same for 40+ stacks before Blade Dance, 30+ stacks before Upper Slash, and so on.
    • If you have 8+ stacks before you activate Death Trance, you can skip both WC precast and SA finisher.
    • At 15+ stacks before Death Trance, you can skip both the WC precast and SA finisher for two cycles in a row.
  4. Surprise Attack always goes before Maelstrom on cycles with a Surprise Attack finisher so its CD aligns.
  5. It seems more complicated than it really is, so watch this video to see how a full rotation plays out.

It helps to think of everything within Death Trance and Deathly Slash as a 53 stack constant, and the chained Wind Cut precast or Surprise Attack finisher as flexible options that give you the 7+ stacks needed to complete a 60+ stack Surge.

All cycles

  1. Depending on attack speed/latency, your Wind Cut precast may grant 7 stacks instead of 8.
  2. It's better to cast a ~59 stack Surge if the alternative is waiting more than 1.5 seconds.
  3. Delaying Deathly Slash + Surge by more than 1.75 seconds to ensure a back attack is a DPS loss.
  4. Delaying only Surge by more than 1 second to ensure a back attack is also a DPS loss.
  5. Blade Assault scales much worse on Surge than on Remaining Energy and takes too long to cast.
    • It's still useful for openers, or it can be saved to greed with push immunity/Hyper Awakening.

Note: The timing to enter Death Trance in cycles without a precast is right as Surge hits. It's unforgiving but it can be improved with a macro that fires the Identity key 2-3x very quickly without any downsides, increasing CPM/QoL.

From 0 orbs

  1. Use a Stimulant (recommended) or proceed to #2.
    • Rat Pack: Use Maelstrom's Orb Control tripod and Flash Blink awakening.
  2. Generate one orb, build at least 40 stacks, then Surge to refill all 3 orbs.

Atropine usage

  1. Use Atropine right before Deathly Slash, and fit two Deathly Slash + Surge pairs in a 10-second window.
  2. Execute your fastest cycles while adapting to your stack count and boss patterns.

docs.title: Rotation
docs.text:
There's an optimal skill order, but you have flexibility when facing downtime or weaving in mobility skills.

Spincutter is your main mobility skill and backup stack builder. Use it to guarantee back attacks on your major skills.

Apply damage synergy if needed, then repeat the rotation cycle as best you can.

From 3 orbs

  1. The final Surprise Attack can often be skipped with surplus stacks and expected raid downtime.
  2. Consider delaying Maelstrom by 1 to 3 skills when uptime drops to ensure it covers Surge (Raid Captain).
  3. Blade Assault scales much worse on Surge than on Remaining Energy and takes too long to cast.
    • It's still useful for Atropine openers, or it can be saved to greed with push immunity/Hyper Awakening.
Alt🐯 Mode

From 0 orbs

  1. Use a Stimulant (recommended) or proceed to #2.
    • Rat Pack: Use Maelstrom's Orb Control tripod and Flash Blink awakening.
  2. Generate one orb, build at least 40 stacks, then Surge to refill all 3 orbs.

docs.text:
3 Orbs›Death Trance›Build Stacks›Surge›↻ repeat

Build toward 60 stacks using your multi-hit skills, then land Surge as a back attack.

The 80-stack cap and rollover give you flexibility. You don't need to stop or force a skill just to hit exactly 60.

Knowing roughly how many stacks each skill generates is important for adapting your rotation.

docs.title: Combat Performance
docs.text:
Surge Casts Per Minute (CPM) and back attack rate are useful measures of how efficiently you cycle Surge.

Only compare CPM between the same encounter and build, as boss uptime and mechanics heavily affect it.
